title: Facebook Ads on a Budget: What £5–£50 a Day Gets You (UK)

facts.fact: The page says a workable starting daily budget for a UK small business generating leads is £12-£25 a day, roughly £360-£750 a month.
facts.quote: For a UK small business generating leads, a workable starting budget is

facts.fact: The page says that below about £10 a day a small business can still get enquiries, but too few for costs to be stable week to week.
facts.quote: Below about £10 a day you can still get enquiries, but so few that costs swing week to week

facts.fact: The page says a £5 a day budget should be treated as a test of offer and creative rather than a lead engine.
facts.quote: At £5 a day, treat it as a test of your offer and creative, not a lead engine.

facts.fact: The page's illustrative figures assume a cost per lead of around £20, which it says is in the range it commonly sees for UK local service businesses using lead forms.
facts.quote: These figures assume a cost per lead of around **£20**, which is in the range we commonly see for UK local service businesses using lead forms.

facts.fact: The page states that at a £20 cost per lead, around £140 a day (about £1,000 a week) is needed to reach Meta's roughly 50 conversions a week, which it says is what exits the learning phase on leads.
facts.quote: you’d need around £1,000 a week (roughly £140 a day) to hit Meta’s ~50 conversions a week.

facts.fact: The page says almost no small business spends £140 a day, so almost every small-budget account runs in the 'Learning Limited' state.
facts.quote: Almost no small business spends that, so almost every small-budget account runs “Learning Limited”.

facts.fact: The page says Meta has no minimum monthly spend, only a small daily floor per ad set.
facts.quote: Meta has no minimum monthly spend, only a small daily floor per ad set

facts.fact: The page states Meta's technical floor is about $1 a day per ad set when charged per impression.
facts.quote: about **$1 a day per ad set** if you’re charged per impression

facts.fact: The page states Meta's technical floor is about $5 a day per ad set when charged per click, like or video view.
facts.quote: about **$5 a day** if you’re charged per click, like or video view

facts.fact: The page states Meta's floor for rare events such as app installs or offer claims is around $40 a day per ad set.
facts.quote: around **$40 a day** for rare events like app installs or offer claims

facts.fact: The page says the working daily floor for lead generation is nearer £10-£12 a day, which it distinguishes from Meta's technical minimum.
facts.quote: For lead generation, the working floor is nearer

facts.fact: The page says that to judge an ad on a working minimum budget, you need about three to four weeks of data.
facts.quote: Can you judge the ad? | No. Too little data to tell good from lucky | Yes, after three to four weeks

facts.fact: The page's rule of thumb is to spend at least half the expected cost per lead each day, so that a lead is averaged every couple of days.
facts.unit: % of expected cost per lead per day
facts.quote: Our rule of thumb: spend at least half your expected cost per lead each day

facts.fact: The page says a cost per lead of £40 is common in competitive trades, and under its half-CPL rule that implies a daily floor of £20.
facts.quote: At £40 a lead (common in competitive trades), it’s £20.

facts.fact: The page states that a Meta daily budget is an average rather than a cap, so spend can exceed the daily figure on strong days and fall short on weak ones, balancing across the week.
facts.quote: A daily budget is an average, not a cap.

facts.fact: The page states that Facebook and Instagram ads are bought through the same Ads Manager and share one budget, so the same minimum floor applies to Instagram ads.
facts.quote: The same floor applies to Instagram ads, because Facebook and Instagram ads are bought through the same Ads Manager and share one budget.

facts.fact: The page defines Meta's ad platform as running across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network.
facts.quote: It's Meta's ad platform, running across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network

facts.fact: The page says Meta does change its minimum budget figures from time to time and that they vary by currency.
facts.quote: Meta does change these figures from time to time, and they vary by currency.

facts.fact: The article is dated 11 June 2026 by author Jamie Frazer.
